hero.headline: Iran suspends talks with US after missile strikes and drone downing
hero.body:
Iran has paused its diplomatic communications with the United States after American and Iranian forces exchanged fire over the weekend. U.S. Central Command announced that it intercepted Iranian ballistic missiles targeting American troops stationed in Kuwait. The U.S. military also conducted strikes against Iranian radar and drone installations after Iran shot down an American drone.

The escalation marks a significant setback in what had been an ongoing message exchange between the two countries. The military confrontations occurred as the Trump administration has been pursuing negotiations with Tehran, though the substance and goals of those talks have not been detailed publicly.

President Trump addressed the situation in a post on Truth Social, calling on Democrats and what he termed seemingly unpatriotic Republicans to stop chirping about the Iran negotiations. Trump stated that Iran really wants to make a deal and predicted it will be a good one. He urged lawmakers to allow him to negotiate without pressure from both sides of the aisle.

The fighting represents the most direct military engagement between U.S. and Iranian forces in recent months. American troops remain stationed in Kuwait and other locations throughout the Middle East, where they have faced periodic threats from Iranian-backed forces and direct Iranian military action. The ballistic missile attack targeting those forces prompted the U.S. defensive response.

The suspension of talks raises questions about the path forward for diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran. Iran's decision to halt the message exchange suggests the military confrontations have complicated whatever progress may have been underway. The administration has not indicated how it plans to resume communications or whether it will adjust its approach in light of the military escalation.

cards.headline: Israel Orders Strikes on Hezbollah Stronghold in Beirut
cards.teaser: Benjamin Netanyahu directed the military to target the Dahieh area in response to attacks on Israeli civilians.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered military strikes on Dahieh, a Beirut suburb and known Hezbollah stronghold. The strikes are described as a response to Hezbollah attacks on Israeli civilians.

Dahieh has long served as a center for Hezbollah's operations in Lebanon. Targeting this densely populated area marks a significant escalation in the conflict between Israel and the militant group.

cards.headline: France Seizes Russian Oil Tanker With British Support
cards.teaser: President Macron said a British helicopter assisted in the operation to seize the sanctioned vessel.
cards.body:
France seized the Tagor, a Russian oil tanker subject to international sanctions, in a Sunday operation in the Atlantic Ocean more than 400 nautical miles west of Brittany. President Emmanuel Macron announced the seizure, which involved support from the United Kingdom and other partners.

A British military helicopter assisted during the operation in international waters. The UK Ministry of Defence confirmed its involvement in the enforcement action. The seizure is part of European efforts to combat Russia's "shadow fleet"—vessels attempting to evade international sanctions imposed on Moscow.

cards.headline: Oil prices rise as US and Iran continue military strikes alongside negotiations
cards.teaser: Crude prices climbed after renewed military exchanges between the United States and Iran, even as diplomatic talks continue.
cards.body:
Oil prices climbed to $96 a barrel as the United States and Iran exchanged military strikes. The US struck Iranian military sites over the weekend, while Iran targeted an American airbase used in previous attacks on southern Iran.

The price surge reflects investor concerns about potential supply disruptions from the escalating conflict. However, both countries remain engaged in negotiations aimed at a more durable ceasefire agreement. The ongoing war has already caused significant global economic disruption, with European manufacturers reporting the largest jump in input costs in four years, driven by rising energy prices and supply chain delays.

cards.headline: Ethiopia Holds Election Amid Fears of Renewed Tigray Conflict
cards.teaser: The vote comes as the country faces tensions with Eritrea over Red Sea access and concerns about fighting in Tigray.
cards.body:
Ethiopia is holding national elections amid significant tensions. The vote takes place as concerns grow about renewed conflict in the Tigray region, where a devastating war ended in a ceasefire.

Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's party is expected to dominate the election. The country also faces tensions with neighboring Eritrea over access to the Red Sea, with ongoing conflicts overshadowing the electoral process.

cards.headline: mRNA vaccine shows high effectiveness against melanoma recurrence
cards.teaser: A study found an mRNA vaccine highly effective at preventing the return of melanoma when combined with the immunotherapy drug Keytruda.
cards.body:
A personalized mRNA vaccine designed specifically for each patient's cancer has proven highly effective at preventing melanoma from returning. When combined with the immunotherapy drug Keytruda, the vaccine significantly reduces recurrence risk in this dangerous skin cancer that can spread throughout the body.

The findings demonstrate a new application for mRNA technology, which became widely known through COVID-19 vaccine development. This research expands understanding of how mRNA-based therapies can be adapted to treat cancer, not just prevent infectious diseases.

hero.headline: Israel Orders Strikes on Hezbollah Stronghold in Beirut

cards.headline: Explosion Kills Dozens in Rebel-Held Myanmar Village
cards.teaser: Local authorities said the blast was an accident at a warehouse storing mining explosives.
cards.body:
An explosion destroyed a village in rebel-controlled Myanmar, killing dozens of people. Local authorities attributed the blast to an accident at a warehouse storing explosives for mining operations.

The incident occurred in territory held by rebel forces opposing Myanmar's military government. The explosion caused widespread destruction across the village.

cards.headline: Ethiopia Holds Election Amid Fears of Renewed Tigray Conflict
cards.teaser: The vote comes as the country faces tensions with Eritrea over Red Sea access and concerns about fighting in Tigray.
cards.body:
Ethiopia is holding national elections amid significant tensions. The vote takes place as concerns grow about renewed conflict in the Tigray region, where a devastating war ended in a ceasefire.

Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's party is expected to dominate the election. The country also faces tensions with neighboring Eritrea over access to the Red Sea, with ongoing conflicts overshadowing the electoral process.

cards.headline: Rescuers Search for Two Missing in Flooded Laos Cave
cards.teaser: Search teams are looking for alternative routes after rescuers reported hearing knocking sounds from inside the cave.
cards.body:
Rescue operations continue in Laos after five men were successfully freed from a flooded cave system. Two miners remain trapped inside the narrow, water-filled tunnels as divers work through hazardous conditions, navigating muddy water and sharp rocks to reach them.

The rescue effort has proven perilous, requiring teams to drain water from the cave and manage collapse risks. Survivors who were freed are assisting rescuers in developing strategies to locate the last two missing men. Rescuers have identified a newly discovered shaft as a potential alternative route to access the area where the trapped individuals are believed to be.

cards.headline: Syrian Regime Officials Face War Crimes Trial in Austria
cards.teaser: Two Assad regime officers are being tried in Austria's first prosecution of Syrian government officials.
cards.body:
Austria is prosecuting two Syrian regime officers in its first war crimes trial against Assad officials. The defendants allegedly operated openly for years before facing charges in an Austrian court.

The trial marks a significant development in international accountability for Syrian civil war atrocities. It allows Syrian witnesses to directly confront the two men they have accused of torture, while demonstrating Europe's growing use of universal jurisdiction laws to prosecute war crimes committed abroad.

cards.headline: Colombia Presidential Election Heads to Runoff Vote
cards.teaser: Abelardo de la Espriella will face a leftist senator in a second round of voting.
cards.body:
Colombia's presidential election will proceed to a runoff after the first round produced no majority winner. Far-right candidate Abelardo de la Espriella secured 43.7% of the vote, narrowly edging out left-wing senator Iván Cepeda, who received 40.9%. The runoff is scheduled for June 21.

Cepeda, a philosopher and human rights activist who has served as a senator since 2014, is backed by outgoing President Gustavo Petro's left-wing party. De la Espriella, a lawyer and Trump admirer, has risen rapidly in the polls. The second round will determine Colombia's next president and shape the country's political direction.

hero.headline: Airlines propose shared blacklist for disruptive passengers
hero.teaser: A new proposal would allow airlines to share information about abusive passengers and restrict their access to flights across multiple carriers.
hero.body:
Airlines are proposing a system to share information about disruptive passengers across the industry. Under the scheme, travelers blacklisted by one airline for abusive behavior could face flight restrictions with multiple carriers, creating a coordinated approach to handling passengers who pose safety or security concerns.

Currently, each airline maintains its own separate list of banned passengers. The new proposal would allow the industry to work together to prevent problem travelers from simply switching to another carrier after being removed from one airline's flights.

cards.headline: Israel orders strikes on Beirut suburbs as Hezbollah conflict intensifies
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu directed the military to target the Hezbollah stronghold of Dahieh in response to attacks on Israeli civilians.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered military strikes on Dahieh, a Hezbollah stronghold in Beirut's southern suburbs. The strikes are in response to attacks on Israeli civilians by the Lebanese militant group.

Dahieh has long served as a base for Hezbollah, which functions as both a political party in Lebanon and a militant organization. The area has been targeted in previous Israeli military operations, and these latest strikes represent an escalation in the periodic conflict between Israel and the Iran-backed group.

cards.headline: Six people stabbed near Arsenal victory parade route in London
cards.teaser: Police arrested 24 people along or near the parade route after six people were stabbed during celebrations.
cards.body:
Six people were stabbed during or after Arsenal's victory parade in London. The Metropolitan Police made 24 arrests along or near the parade route. The violence occurred as fans gathered to celebrate the team's championship win.

The stabbings took place amid large crowds that had assembled for the parade. Police presence was increased following the incidents. Authorities are investigating the circumstances that led to the violence during what was intended as a celebratory event for the football club and its supporters.

cards.headline: mRNA vaccine shows high effectiveness against melanoma recurrence

A personalized mRNA vaccine designed specifically for each patient's cancer has proven highly effective at preventing melanoma from returning. cards.headline: Girl, 13, dies after river rescue in Yorkshire Dales
cards.teaser: Police said the girl went missing in the river near the village of Burnsall and later died in the hospital.
cards.body:
A 13-year-old girl has died in hospital after being rescued from a river in the Yorkshire Dales. Police said she went missing in the water near Burnsall, a village in North Yorkshire, and emergency services pulled her from the river.

The girl was taken to hospital for treatment but died from her injuries. Burnsall is located along the River Wharfe, which flows through the Yorkshire Dales National Park and is a popular destination for visitors.

cards.headline: UK court rules against Rwanda payment for collapsed asylum deal
cards.teaser: A court decided the UK does not need to pay Rwanda after the government pulled out of a deal to send asylum seekers to the African nation.
cards.body:
An international court has ruled that the UK does not owe Rwanda payment following the collapse of their asylum deal. Rwanda had sued the British government for over £100 million, claiming breach of the agreement after the scheme was scrapped.

The Rwanda plan was a centerpiece of the previous government's immigration policy, which would have seen asylum seekers processed in the east African nation. The Labour government abandoned the arrangement on its first day in office, prompting Rwanda's legal action.

hero.headline: UAW strikes at General Motors supplier plant over stagnant wages
hero.body:
The United Auto Workers union launched a strike at midnight at American Axle & Manufacturing, a critical supplier that produces axles for General Motors pickup trucks. The work stoppage threatens production of GM's profitable truck line at a Michigan facility where employees say wages have barely increased over 18 years.

The strike targets a plant in southwest Michigan that supplies essential components for GM pickup production. American Axle employees walked off the job after the union called for the midnight strike. The action puts pressure on GM's truck manufacturing operations, which depend on a steady flow of axles and related parts from the supplier facility.

Workers at the plant have expressed frustration over compensation that they say has remained largely flat for nearly two decades. The wage stagnation has become a central issue in the labor dispute. The UAW represents workers at American Axle facilities and has made pay increases a priority in negotiations with the supplier.

General Motors relies heavily on American Axle as a supplier for its pickup truck production, making the strike a potential disruption to one of the automaker's most profitable vehicle segments. Pickup trucks generate significant revenue for GM, and any extended production halt could affect the company's financial performance. The strike also comes at a time when the auto industry faces broader pressures from supply chain management and labor costs.

The UAW has not announced the duration of the strike or specific demands beyond wage increases. American Axle and the union will need to reach an agreement to resume normal production operations. GM has not publicly commented on how the strike will affect its truck manufacturing schedule or whether it has contingency plans to maintain production during the work stoppage.

The strike reflects broader tensions within the automotive industry over worker compensation and labor practices. Major automakers have faced increased scrutiny in recent years over various operational practices. This includes concerns from regulators and consumers about how companies handle sensitive driver information and protect consumer privacy.

The labor action at American Axle comes as the auto industry continues to navigate complex challenges related to supply chains, production costs, and labor relations. Both the union and the supplier will be working toward a resolution that addresses worker concerns while maintaining production timelines for GM's truck operations.

The outcome of this strike could have implications for labor negotiations across the automotive supply chain. Other suppliers and manufacturers may face similar wage-related demands from their workforces as the industry grapples with inflation and worker expectations for improved compensation after years of minimal increases.

cards.headline: Oil prices rise as US and Iran continue military strikes alongside negotiations
cards.teaser: Crude prices climbed after renewed military exchanges between the United States and Iran, even as diplomatic talks continue.

Oil prices climbed to $96 a barrel as the United States and Iran exchanged military strikes. The US struck Iranian military sites over the weekend, while Iran targeted an American airbase used in previous attacks on southern Iran.

cards.headline: Barry Diller preparing $18 billion takeover bid for MGM Resorts
cards.teaser: Media mogul Barry Diller's People Inc. is preparing an offer to acquire the portion of MGM Resorts it does not already own.
cards.body:
Barry Diller's People Inc. is moving to acquire full control of MGM Resorts in a transaction valued at $18 billion. The company already holds a stake in the casino operator and is now seeking to buy the remaining portion.

The proposed acquisition has drawn positive market reaction, with MGM Resorts stock rising on news of the potential bid.

cards.headline: Berkshire Hathaway acquires homebuilder Taylor Morrison for $8.5 billion
cards.teaser: The purchase marks the first major acquisition under CEO Greg Abel following Warren Buffett's departure.
cards.body:
Berkshire Hathaway completed its first major acquisition under CEO Greg Abel, purchasing homebuilder Taylor Morrison for $8.5 billion. The deal marks a significant milestone for Abel since taking over leadership from Warren Buffett.

Buffett publicly endorsed Abel's dealmaking on the transaction, expressing confidence in the new CEO's investment approach. The acquisition adds Taylor Morrison's residential homebuilding operations across multiple markets to Berkshire's expanding business portfolio.

cards.headline: Nvidia introduces new AI chip designed for personal computers
cards.teaser: The technology company released a processor aimed at bringing artificial intelligence capabilities to consumer PCs.
cards.body:
Nvidia announced a new artificial intelligence chip tailored for personal computers. CEO Jensen Huang called the product a "reinvention of the computer," positioning it to bring AI processing directly to consumer devices rather than relying on cloud-based solutions.

The announcement boosted market sentiment around AI technology and contributed to gains in Nvidia's stock price. The company continues to establish itself as a leader in processors designed for artificial intelligence, targeting the personal computer market as AI features become increasingly integrated into consumer software.

cards.headline: Wise under investigation by Brussels prosecutor over money laundering controls
cards.teaser: The money transfer company said it is cooperating with Belgian authorities but has not received specific findings.
cards.body:
Money transfer service Wise is cooperating with the Brussels prosecutor's office in an investigation concerning its money laundering controls. The company confirmed it is working with investigators on the matter.

Wise said that no specific findings have been shared with the company to date. The fintech platform facilitates international money transfers for customers sending funds across borders.

cards.headline: Airlines could share passenger blacklists under new proposal
cards.teaser: A proposed system would allow carriers to exchange information about disruptive passengers and potentially restrict their flight access.
cards.body:
A new proposal would allow airlines to share information about disruptive passengers, potentially enabling carriers to restrict their access to flights across the industry. The scheme aims to coordinate responses to abusive behavior on flights through data-sharing among participating airlines.

Rather than limiting consequences to a single airline, passengers identified as disruptive could face booking restrictions with multiple carriers in the program. This coordinated approach would create a shared industry response to passenger misconduct.

hero.headline: Meteor explodes over Massachusetts, prompts reports across Northeast
hero.body:
A meteor exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, creating a massive blast that generated loud booms heard across a wide region. NASA confirmed the event occurred just after 2pm local time, with the fireball breaking apart at an altitude of 40 miles above the earth's surface.

The meteor was traveling at 75,000 miles per hour when it fragmented in the atmosphere. The explosion produced a blast equivalent to 300 tons of TNT, according to NASA's deputy news chief Jennifer Dooren. The American Meteor Society reported that the meteor was approximately 3 feet wide as it entered the atmosphere near the New Hampshire and Massachusetts border, north of Boston.

Reports of the explosion came from across a wide geographic area. People from Delaware to Montreal reported hearing the loud booms or witnessing the bright fireball crossing the sky. The sonic boom traveled considerable distances from the explosion site, demonstrating the significant force of the atmospheric impact.

NASA indicated that fragments from the meteor may have landed in Cape Cod Bay. The space agency suggested that pieces of meteorite could potentially be recovered from the bay area, offering valuable opportunities for scientific study. Meteorites that survive atmospheric entry and reach the surface provide researchers with direct samples of material from space.

When meteors enter Earth's atmosphere at high speeds, friction causes them to heat rapidly. The intense heat and pressure can cause the object to fragment or explode, creating the sonic booms heard by observers on the ground. According to NASA's website, most space rocks smaller than a football field will break apart in Earth's atmosphere, though on rare occasions they may explode in the air.

Approximately 17,000 meteorites fall to Earth annually, yet events visible and audible across such a wide geographic area remain relatively uncommon. The Saturday explosion represents a notable example of a significant atmospheric impact witnessed by many residents across the Northeast.

NASA continues to analyze data from the event to better understand the meteor's size, composition, and trajectory. Recovery efforts for meteorite fragments could provide valuable scientific information about the object's origins and composition. Such samples help scientists understand the makeup of asteroids and materials from the early solar system.

The event generated widespread attention and numerous reports from residents throughout the region who were startled by the bright flash and audible explosion. Local authorities received multiple calls from people reporting the phenomenon, and the meteor event sparked considerable discussion on social media as people shared their experiences of witnessing the spectacular event.

cards.headline: OpenAI model solves 80-year-old mathematics problem
cards.teaser: An artificial intelligence model from OpenAI has solved a famous mathematics problem that remained unsolved for eight decades.
cards.body:
OpenAI announced that one of its models successfully solved a longstanding mathematics problem that had stumped mathematicians for 80 years. The company released an explanation of the solution, attempting to make the mathematical breakthrough more accessible to general audiences.

The achievement represents a significant milestone in AI's ability to tackle complex theoretical problems. The specific nature of the mathematical problem and the details of the solution method demonstrate the advancing capabilities of AI systems in abstract reasoning and problem-solving domains that previously required human mathematical expertise.

cards.headline: Nvidia launches first PC processor to compete with Apple Silicon
cards.teaser: Nvidia introduced its first processor designed for personal computers, entering direct competition with Apple's Silicon chips.
cards.body:
Nvidia announced a new processor designed for Windows PCs, marking the company's entry into the consumer PC chip market. The move positions Nvidia as a direct competitor to Apple's Silicon processors, which have powered Mac computers since 2020. Multiple PC manufacturers have already adopted the new chip for upcoming products.

The announcement coincided with broader market movement in technology stocks. Shares of Arm, IBM, and Hewlett Packard rose following Nvidia's chip introduction, which analysts characterized as a reinvention that extends a rally in software-related stocks. ServiceNow and Adobe also saw stock increases tied to the AI chip announcement.

cards.headline: Dell launches $599 laptop to challenge Apple MacBook Neo
cards.teaser: Dell introduced a new XPS 13 laptop priced at $599, positioning it as a budget alternative to Apple's MacBook Neo.
cards.body:
Dell announced a new XPS 13 laptop designed to compete with Apple's MacBook Neo. The device will launch in July with a promotional price of $599 for students, available through September for back-to-school shopping. After the introductory period ends, the standard price rises to $699.

The XPS 13 features an Nvidia PC chip as an alternative to Apple Silicon. Dell's strategy targets budget-conscious consumers looking for a Windows-based alternative to Apple's ecosystem at a lower price point.

cards.headline: Student astronomer discovers key to understanding mysterious space signals
cards.teaser: A student astronomer found what scientists are calling a Rosetta Stone for decoding puzzling cosmic signals that have baffled researchers.
cards.body:
A student researcher discovered a celestial object that scientists believe provides crucial insight into mysterious periodic signals coming from space. The finding, published in Nature, identifies ASKAP J1745-5051 as a white dwarf binary system that emits both radio and X-ray signals on predictable timescales. Researchers describe the discovery as a Rosetta Stone that could help decode similar baffling signals from deep space.

The white dwarf binary system produces periodic radio bursts lasting hours, a pattern that has puzzled astronomers studying similar signals from other cosmic sources. The discovery links these hour-scale radio emissions to the behavior of accreting white dwarf systems, providing a framework for understanding comparable phenomena throughout the universe.

cards.headline: Microsoft confirms outage affecting authentication services
cards.teaser: Microsoft acknowledged a service disruption impacting multi-factor authentication and its My Sign-Ins platform.
cards.body:
Microsoft confirmed an outage affecting its multi-factor authentication system and the My Sign-Ins platform. The service disruption prevented users from accessing authentication features required for logging into various Microsoft services and third-party applications that rely on Microsoft's identity infrastructure.

The outage impacted businesses and individual users who depend on Microsoft's authentication systems for security. Multi-factor authentication serves as a critical security layer for protecting accounts, requiring users to verify their identity through multiple methods beyond just passwords.

cards.headline: Asus announces first 24.5-inch OLED monitor with 540Hz refresh rate
cards.teaser: Asus unveiled the first OLED esports monitor in the 24.5-inch size category, featuring a 540Hz refresh rate.
cards.body:
Asus and its Republic of Gamers division announced the ROG Strix OLED XG259QWPG Ace, marking the first time a 24.5-inch OLED panel has been used in an esports-focused monitor. The display offers a 540Hz refresh rate, targeting competitive gaming applications where high frame rates provide advantages. The company also previewed a 720Hz ROG Swift OLED monitor.

The 24.5-inch form factor has been popular among esports professionals who prefer smaller screens for competitive gaming.

hero.headline: Hall of Fame receiver Raymond Berry dies at 93
hero.body:
Raymond Berry, a Hall of Fame receiver who starred for the Baltimore Colts and later coached the New England Patriots, has died at 93. Berry's career spanned both sides of the game, leaving a lasting impact on professional football.

Berry earned his place in Canton by leading the NFL in receptions three times during his playing career with the Colts. His precise route running and reliable hands made him one of the most effective receivers of his era, helping define the position for future generations.

After retiring as a player, Berry transitioned to coaching and took the helm of the Patriots. His coaching tenure added another dimension to his football legacy, demonstrating his deep understanding of the game from multiple perspectives.

Berry's career bridged different eras of professional football, from his playing days with the Colts through his coaching years with New England. His contributions to the sport earned him recognition as one of the game's all-time greats, with his Hall of Fame induction cementing his place in football history.

The death of the 93-year-old removes another link to the earlier decades of the NFL, when the league was still establishing the passing game as a central element of modern football. Berry's success as both a player who mastered receiving and a coach who could teach the game represents a complete football life.

cards.headline: French Open fines player $76,000 for sexist remark about umpire
cards.teaser: Paraguay's Adolfo Daniel Vallejo must pay half his French Open prize money after saying his match should not have been umpired by a woman.
cards.body:
Paraguay's Adolfo Daniel Vallejo has been fined roughly $65,000 by the French Open for comments he made during his second-round match. The penalty equals half of his prize money from the tournament.

Vallejo stated that his match should not have been umpired by a woman. The fine represents one of the larger financial penalties the tournament has issued for conduct violations.

cards.headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander calls MVP season a failure after Thunder elimination
cards.teaser: The Thunder star said his second straight MVP award means little after Oklahoma City was eliminated before reaching the NBA Finals.
cards.body:
Despite winning his second consecutive NBA MVP award, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander expressed disappointment with his season after the Thunder fell short of the Finals. He characterized the year as a failure, prioritizing team success over individual recognition.

Oklahoma City's playoff run ended before they could defend their title in the championship round. Gilgeous-Alexander's assessment underscores his belief that winning matters more than personal accolades, regardless of individual achievements.

cards.headline: Saint Mary's eliminates top-seeded UCLA from NCAA baseball tournament
cards.teaser: Makoa Sniffen's 10th-inning single knocked out the 51-6 Bruins in an upset victory in Los Angeles.
cards.body:
Saint Mary's pulled off a stunning upset, defeating top-seeded UCLA 6-5 in 10 innings on Sunday in Los Angeles. Makoa Sniffen delivered the decisive blow with a run-scoring single in the extra inning, eliminating the Bruins from the NCAA baseball tournament.

The victory was particularly improbable given UCLA's impressive regular season. The Bruins entered the weekend with a 51-6 record and were among the tournament favorites.

cards.headline: Blue Jays outfielder injured by ball thrown from stands
cards.teaser: Jesus Sanchez left Sunday's game against the Orioles after being hit on the wrist by a ball thrown by a fan.
cards.body:
Blue Jays outfielder Jesus Sánchez exited Sunday's game against the Orioles after being struck on the wrist by a ball thrown from the stands. The injury forced him to leave the game.

The incident highlights ongoing safety concerns for players during games when objects are thrown from the crowd.

cards.headline: Illinois delays Bears stadium vote until fall
cards.teaser: State lawmakers adjourned their spring session without voting on a bill to keep the Chicago Bears in Illinois.
cards.body:
Illinois lawmakers concluded their spring session without passing legislation aimed at keeping the Chicago Bears from relocating out of state. The vote has been postponed until fall, leaving the team's future location uncertain for several more months.

The Bears say they plan to announce their decision soon about where they will play in the future. The delayed legislative action means the team may make its choice before Illinois can offer a formal incentive package to retain the franchise.

cards.headline: Bryce Harper voices concern over potential 2027 lockout
cards.teaser: The Phillies star warned against losing momentum if labor negotiations compromise next season.
cards.body:
Bryce Harper expressed concern about the potential impact on baseball if the 2027 season is affected by a lockout. The Phillies star addressed the ongoing labor situation between players and owners as negotiations continue.

Harper specifically warned about losing momentum in the sport if next season is compromised. His comments highlight player concerns about the state of labor talks heading into a period when the current collective bargaining situation could affect the upcoming season.

hero.headline: A24 horror film Backrooms opens to $118 million worldwide
hero.body:
Kane Parsons has made history as the youngest filmmaker to open a movie at number one at the North American box office. The 20-year-old YouTube creator's directorial debut, Backrooms, earned $81 million domestically and $118 million worldwide in its opening weekend, shattering industry expectations and setting a new studio record for A24.

Parsons surpassed the previous record holder Josh Trank, who was 27 when his 2011 debut Chronicle opened with $22 million. The scale of Backrooms' performance demonstrates a dramatic generational shift in how quickly young creators can transition from digital platforms to major studio releases.

The film adapts Parsons' web series concept for theatrical audiences. A24 tapped screenwriter Will Soodik to develop the feature, bringing Parsons' online horror concept to mainstream cinemas. The production design combines physical construction with digital effects to create vast, unsettling spaces. Cinematographer Jeremy Cox shot the film using a distinctive yellowish light that evokes the fluorescent glow of shopping malls and office buildings.

The cast includes Chiwetel Ejiofor as Clark, a failed architect and struggling manager of a discount furniture store, and Renate Reinsve as Mary, his therapist. The story centers on Clark's discovery of a supernatural section of wall in his store's basement that leads to an infinite network of mysterious rooms. As both characters venture deeper into this strange space, they struggle to find their way back.

The film's success exceeded what observers anticipated for a debut feature from an internet creator. A24 has built its reputation releasing art house and horror films, but had never achieved an opening weekend at this scale. The previous studio record was set by Alex Garland's 2024 film, which Backrooms more than tripled.

A24's decision to release Backrooms in wide theatrical distribution rather than limiting it to specialty venues proved strategically sound. Strong ticket sales came from audiences across the country and internationally, suggesting that Parsons' appeal extends beyond his core YouTube fanbase of English-speaking viewers.

The opening weekend performance suggests studios may pursue other internet creators with significant digital followings as potential theatrical filmmakers. Backrooms demonstrates genuine audience appetite for horror content and the commercial viability of creators who build substantial fan communities online before transitioning to traditional filmmaking.

Parsons' achievement underscores how digital platforms have created alternative pathways to studio filmmaking. Where previous generations of directors needed to work through film school or traditional industry channels, creators like Parsons can now build large enough followings to attract major studio attention directly. The box office numbers suggest audiences are willing to support films from creators they already follow online when given the theatrical opportunity.

cards.headline: CBS cancels The Late Show with Stephen Colbert
cards.teaser: Jimmy Kimmel called the cancellation part of a broader decline in late-night television that he says is not happening naturally.
cards.body:
CBS canceled The Late Show with Stephen Colbert, ending the long-running late-night program. Jimmy Kimmel discussed the cancellation in an interview with Vulture, describing himself as feeling defeated by the news.

Kimmel argued that late-night television is facing an unnatural decline. He said the genre is being poisoned rather than dying of natural causes. Kimmel also addressed his own run-ins with Trump and mentioned being suspended following comments he made about the president.

cards.headline: Dua Lipa marries Callum Turner in London
cards.teaser: The singer and actor wed at Old Marylebone Town Hall after two years together.
cards.body:
Dua Lipa married actor Callum Turner at Old Marylebone Town Hall in London. The couple have been in a relationship since 2024.

The ceremony took place at the historic London venue. Old Marylebone Town Hall has hosted numerous celebrity weddings over the years. The couple kept the wedding low-key rather than staging a large public event.

cards.headline: Charli xcx announces album Music, Fashion, Film for July release
cards.teaser: The singer revealed her seventh studio album will arrive July 24 with a cover featuring Martin Scorsese, John Cale, and Marc Jacobs.
cards.body:
Charli xcx has unveiled her seventh studio album, Music, Fashion, Film, arriving July 24. The singer made the surprise announcement on Monday by sharing the album cover on Instagram, bypassing a traditional promotional rollout.

The cover showcases a black-and-white photograph featuring director Martin Scorsese, musician John Cale, and designer Marc Jacobs—each representing the three titular elements of the album.

cards.headline: Rosamund Pike calls out audience member for texting during West End performance
cards.teaser: The actress addressed someone using their phone at the end of her performance in the play Inter Alia.
cards.body:
Rosamund Pike confronted an audience member who was texting during her West End performance. The actress called out the person at the end of the show in Inter Alia.

Pike told the audience member "you know who you are" when addressing the incident. The actress was performing at a West End theater in London. Theater etiquette typically prohibits phone use during live performances due to the distraction caused by lit screens.

cards.headline: HBO releases docuseries on cult that recruited models
cards.teaser: Director Chris Smith and former member Hoyt Richards discuss a new series about Eternal Values and its leader.
cards.body:
HBO released the miniseries "Bring Me the Beauties," a documentary about Eternal Values, a cult founded in the 1980s by Frederick von Mierers. The group primarily recruited models with promises of enlightenment. Director Chris Smith, known for documentaries including the 1999 film "American Movie" and Netflix projects on Jim Carrey and the Fyre festival, helmed the series.

Smith discovered the story through Hoyt Richards, considered the first male supermodel and a former Eternal Values member, whom he met while working on another project. Richards' detailed accounts of his experience in the cult sparked Smith's interest in exploring how the organization operated and maintained control over its members.

cards.headline: Roots Picnic draws performances from Erykah Badu and Kehlani in Philadelphia
cards.teaser: The Roots staged their annual festival at Belmont Plateau with two days of hip-hop and R&B acts.
cards.body:
The Roots held their annual Roots Picnic festival at Belmont Plateau in Philadelphia. The lineup included performances from Erykah Badu, Kehlani, De La Soul, and T.I. across two days.

Questlove, Black Thought, and the rest of the Roots organized the festival, which has been running for almost a decade. The event featured hip-hop and R&B artists performing seamlessly over the weekend. The hometown Philadelphia crew assembled what organizers described as the best of both genres for the festival.

hero.headline: Iran suspends talks with US after missile strikes and drone downing
hero.body:
Iran has paused its diplomatic communications with the United States after American and Iranian forces exchanged fire over the weekend. U.S. Central Command announced that it intercepted Iranian ballistic missiles targeting American troops stationed in Kuwait. The U.S. military also conducted strikes against Iranian radar and drone installations after Iran shot down an American drone.

The escalation marks a significant setback in what had been an ongoing message exchange between the two countries. The military confrontations occurred as the Trump administration has been pursuing negotiations with Tehran, though the substance and goals of those talks have not been detailed publicly.

President Trump addressed the situation in a post on Truth Social, calling on Democrats and what he termed seemingly unpatriotic Republicans to stop chirping about the Iran negotiations. Trump stated that Iran really wants to make a deal and predicted it will be a good one. He urged lawmakers to allow him to negotiate without pressure from both sides of the aisle.

The fighting represents the most direct military engagement between U.S. and Iranian forces in recent months. American troops remain stationed in Kuwait and other locations throughout the Middle East, where they have faced periodic threats from Iranian-backed forces and direct Iranian military action. The ballistic missile attack targeting those forces prompted the U.S. defensive response.

The suspension of talks raises questions about the path forward for diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran. Iran's decision to halt the message exchange suggests the military confrontations have complicated whatever progress may have been underway. The administration has not indicated how it plans to resume communications or whether it will adjust its approach in light of the military escalation.

cards.headline: Former Colorado elections clerk Tina Peters to be released from prison
cards.teaser: Tina Peters, the first local official convicted over efforts to subvert the 2020 presidential election, will leave prison after Colorado's governor commuted her sentence.
cards.body:
Tina Peters, a former Colorado elections clerk, is being released from prison after Governor Jared Polis commuted her sentence. Peters was the first local official convicted in connection with efforts to subvert the 2020 presidential election, and her case drew national attention as prosecutors pursued charges against election officials involved in attempts to overturn election results.

Peters served less than a quarter of her original nine-year sentence before the commutation was granted. She is set to be released on Monday.

cards.headline: Arrests follow curfew enforcement at ICE detention facility in New Jersey
cards.teaser: New Jersey's attorney general responded after arrests were made when some people refused to comply with a curfew around an Immigration and Customs Enforcement facility.
cards.body:
Family visitation has been partially restored at Delaney Hall immigration detention center after a week of protests sparked by a detainee hunger strike. Governor Mikie Sherrill and US Department of Homeland Security officials announced the resumption of visits on Sunday morning.

Local officials imposed an overnight curfew beginning at 9pm around the facility in response to the demonstrations. Arrests followed after the curfew took effect, prompting attention from New Jersey's attorney general.

cards.headline: House and Senate Republicans face stalled midterm agenda
cards.teaser: GOP leaders return to find their midterm-year legislative agenda threatened by familiar problems, including disputes over Trump fund allocations.
cards.body:
House and Senate Republican leaders are confronting obstacles that threaten to stall their legislative agenda ahead of the midterm elections. The problems facing GOP leadership are not new, but continue to create difficulties for advancing their policy priorities.

Angst over Trump fund allocations is among the issues keeping the Republican agenda in limbo. The disputes reflect ongoing tensions within the party over how to allocate resources and prioritize legislative goals as the midterm election year progresses.

cards.headline: Maine Senate candidate's wife defends husband over sexting reports
cards.teaser: Amy Gertner called media coverage of her husband Graham Platner's reported past sexting with multiple women shameful gossip that distracts from serious issues.
cards.body:
Amy Gertner, wife of Maine Senate Democratic candidate Graham Platner, released a video addressing reports of her husband's past sexting with multiple women. She called the coverage "shameful" and characterized it as gossip that distracts from substantive policy issues in the Senate race.

Gertner and Platner married in 2023 and live together in Sullivan with two dogs. In the video, she attempted to redirect public attention away from the personal allegations and toward the candidate's policy positions.

cards.headline: President Trump plans birthday celebration with military displays and UFC
cards.teaser: President Trump is using large-scale events featuring military displays, fireworks, and UFC to rally political support for his administration.
cards.body:
President Trump is organizing a series of events to celebrate his birthday and build political support for his administration. The celebrations will feature military displays, fireworks, and statues of historical figures, along with UFC entertainment.

The president is using the birthday celebration as an opportunity to rally his political base. Some performers scheduled for a related concert raised concerns about the event's political nature and dropped out of the lineup.

cards.headline: Google seeks approval to release millions of mosquitoes in California and Florida
cards.teaser: The technology company wants to release up to 32 million mosquitoes in two states as part of a program involving actual insects rather than software bugs.
cards.body:
Google is seeking permission to release up to 32 million mosquitoes in California and Florida. The initiative represents an unusual venture for the technology company, which typically focuses on software and digital products.

The mosquito release program marks a departure from Google's typical debugging work, which involves fixing software errors. The company has not released details about the purpose of the mosquito release or what makes these insects different from wild populations.
